identity.name: Cloud Workload IAM Usage Anomaly — Cortex Analytics Behavioral IOC (ABIOC) (T1078.004 / T1580)
identity.summary: A cloud workload identity (an EC2 instance role) whose learned Cortex baseline is a narrow, low-rate set of API actions suddenly issues a burst of calls and a set of actions it has never invoked — the CloudTrail shape of post-compromise credential abuse. No single call is a known-bad IOC; the ABIOC fires on the deviation from the role's learned IAM usage baseline plus its causality chain.
identity.description: Analytics Behavioral IOC (ABIOC) is a first-party Cortex detection type distinct from a hand-authored BIOC: PANW authors and continually tunes ABIOCs against the user, endpoint, and network behavioral profiles Cortex learns per environment, firing on a single suspicious event that carries an identified chain of causality. This scenario exercises that detector class on the CLOUD/CDR plane against an IAM workload identity — the credential-theft gap Unit 42 documents where a stolen or exposed instance-role credential is driven far outside the workload's learned behavior. Cortex Cloud / CDR ingests the CloudTrail audit stream and learns that a given assumed-role session (the EC2 instance profile behind an application) makes a small, stable set of API calls at a low, steady rate — a handful of s3:GetObject / dynamodb:Query calls the application needs, and nothing else. This scenario injects two behavioral deviations from that learned baseline against the sandboxed lab role: (a) an API-call-rate spike — dozens of calls in a short window from an identity whose baseline is a few calls per hour, and (b) a new-action-set deviation — Discovery and IAM actions (sts:GetCallerIdentity, iam:ListUsers, iam:ListRoles, ec2:DescribeInstances, s3api:ListBuckets) the role has never invoked in its learned profile, the canonical leaked-credential enumeration burst. A hand-authored BIOC keyed on a specific bad API name would miss this — every action is a legitimate AWS call an admin makes daily — which is exactly the point: the auto-tuned ABIOC fires on the deviation from the identity's learned usage baseline and anchors it to the causality chain (assumed-role session -> anomalous call-rate + new-action fan-out from a source/agent new for this identity). Two ABIOCs cover the two deviation shapes; supporting validation XQL confirms the baseline identity and surfaces the new-action deviation; a correlation rule stitches the two ABIOCs into a single compromised-workload-credential incident the DC presents as proof that Cortex's behavioral analytics caught post-compromise credential abuse no static rule was written for.

actors.name: Opportunistic cloud intruders abusing stolen or exposed workload credentials

campaigns: Leaked cloud-credential abuse — enumerate then exfiltrate against exposed IAM identities (2022-2026)

execution.framework_reference_id: SIM-CDR-016 — Cloud workload IAM usage anomaly (call-rate + new-action deviation) for Cortex ABIOC validation

prerequisites.description: Cortex XSIAM / Cortex Cloud CDR ingesting the AWS CloudTrail audit stream into cloud_audit_logs so per-identity API usage is profiled.
A baseline window has elapsed during which the lab workload role made only its narrow, low-rate application API calls so Cortex learned the identity usage profile.

payload.code:
# No known-bad payloads. Drive a learned cloud workload identity far outside its
# learned IAM usage baseline: an API-call-rate spike plus a new-action-set burst.
set -euo pipefail
AWS_PROFILE_ARG="${AWS_PROFILE:+--profile $AWS_PROFILE}"
LAB_REGION="${LAB_REGION:-us-east-1}"
if command -v aws >/dev/null 2>&1 && aws sts get-caller-identity $AWS_PROFILE_ARG >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  # (a) new-action-set deviation: Discovery/IAM actions the role never invokes
  aws sts get-caller-identity $AWS_PROFILE_ARG >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  aws iam list-users $AWS_PROFILE_ARG >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  aws iam list-roles $AWS_PROFILE_ARG >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  aws ec2 describe-instances --region "$LAB_REGION" $AWS_PROFILE_ARG >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  aws s3api list-buckets $AWS_PROFILE_ARG >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  # (b) call-rate spike: many calls in a short window vs a few-per-hour baseline
  for i in $(seq 1 40); do aws sts get-caller-identity $AWS_PROFILE_ARG >/dev/null 2>&1 || true; done
else
  echo '[*] demo-mode: aws cli not configured — CDR should still flag the call-rate + new-action deviation from the role baseline'
fi

input_variables.name: LAB_REGION
input_variables.description: AWS region the Discovery API burst targets during the deviation.

input_variables.name: AWS_PROFILE
input_variables.description: Optional AWS CLI profile bound to the sandboxed lab workload role.

expected_artifacts.description: A burst of CloudTrail events from an assumed-role session whose learned baseline is a few calls per hour.
expected_artifacts.expected_value: user_identity_type = "AssumedRole" and event count within 5m exceeds learned baseline rate

expected_artifacts.description: Discovery/IAM API actions from the workload role absent from its learned action set.
expected_artifacts.expected_value: event_name in (GetCallerIdentity, ListUsers, ListRoles, DescribeInstances, ListBuckets) new for this identity

cleanup.code: echo '[CortexSim] SIM-CDR-016 cleanup complete — read-only Discovery calls only; rotate the lab role credential between runs.'

abiocs.name: CDR-016 Anomalous IAM API-Call Rate Spike from Baselined Workload Role
abiocs.description: A cloud workload identity whose learned Cortex baseline is a narrow set of API calls at a low, steady rate suddenly issues a burst of calls well above its learned rate within a short window. ABIOC anchors the deviation to the causality chain (assumed-role session -> call-rate spike from a source/agent new for this identity) rather than to any known-bad API name, catching post-compromise credential abuse a static rule keyed on a specific action would miss.
abiocs.logic:
dataset = cloud_audit_logs
| filter cloud_provider = "AWS" and identity_type = "AssumedRole"
| filter _time > to_timestamp(current_time() - 300)
| comp count() as call_count by identity_name, caller_ip
| filter call_count >= 30
| sort desc call_count
| fields identity_name, caller_ip, call_count
abiocs.causality_anchor: Learned workload-identity usage baseline (a few API calls per hour) -> assumed-role session -> API-call-rate spike from a source IP/user-agent new for this identity, anchored to the originating session.

abiocs.name: CDR-016 New-Action-Set Deviation from Learned IAM Usage Baseline
abiocs.description: A workload role whose learned action set is a small, stable list of application API calls suddenly invokes Discovery and IAM actions it has never used in its learned profile. Every action is a legitimate AWS call; the ABIOC fires on the new-action-set deviation from the identity's learned behavior, anchored to the assumed-role session that issued them.
abiocs.logic:
dataset = cloud_audit_logs
| filter cloud_provider = "AWS" and identity_type = "AssumedRole"
| filter operation_name in ("GetCallerIdentity", "ListUsers", "ListRoles", "DescribeInstances", "ListBuckets")
| comp count_distinct(operation_name) as new_actions by identity_name, caller_ip
| filter new_actions >= 3
| sort desc new_actions
| fields identity_name, caller_ip, new_actions
abiocs.causality_anchor: Assumed-role session -> fan-out of Discovery/IAM actions that diverge from the role's learned action set, anchored to the session that first exhibited the new actions.

xql_queries.name: CDR-016 Workload Role IAM Baseline Learned
xql_queries.query:
dataset = cloud_audit_logs
| filter _time > to_timestamp(current_time() - 900)
| filter cloud_provider = "AWS" and identity_type = "AssumedRole"
| comp count_distinct(operation_name) as baseline_actions by identity_name
| filter baseline_actions >= 1
| fields identity_name, baseline_actions

xql_queries.name: CDR-016 New-Action Deviation Surfaced in Cloud Audit Log
xql_queries.query:
dataset = cloud_audit_logs
| filter _time > to_timestamp(current_time() - 900)
| filter cloud_provider = "AWS" and identity_type = "AssumedRole"
| filter operation_name in ("GetCallerIdentity", "ListUsers", "ListRoles", "DescribeInstances", "ListBuckets")
| comp count() as deviation_calls by identity_name
| filter deviation_calls >= 1
| fields identity_name, deviation_calls

correlation_rules.name: Compromised Workload Credential — ABIOC Causality Stitch
correlation_rules.logic: ABIOC(CDR-016 Anomalous IAM API-Call Rate Spike from Baselined Workload Role) AND ABIOC(CDR-016 New-Action-Set Deviation from Learned IAM Usage Baseline) — fuses the two auto-tuned behavioral deviations on the same identity into a single compromised-workload-credential incident anchored to the assumed-role causality chain.

threat_scenarios.name: Cloud Workload IAM Usage Anomaly Detection via Cortex ABIOC
threat_scenarios.description: Cortex's auto-tuned Analytics Behavioral IOCs learn a workload identity's cloud API usage baseline (rate and action set) and detect post-compromise credential abuse anchored to its causality chain, where no static rule was written for the legitimate API calls involved.

threat_steps.objective: Cortex learns the workload-role baseline and an injected usage deviation fires both ABIOCs.
preconditions: Cortex Cloud / CDR ingesting the AWS CloudTrail audit stream.
Baseline window elapsed with the lab role making only its narrow, low-rate application calls.
steps: Let the workload-identity baseline window elapse.
Drive the lab role with a call-rate spike and a Discovery/IAM new-action burst.
Observe both ABIOCs fire and CR-CDR-0016 raise a compromised-workload-credential incident.
success_criteria: ABIOC `CDR-016 Anomalous IAM API-Call Rate Spike from Baselined Workload Role` fires.
ABIOC `CDR-016 New-Action-Set Deviation from Learned IAM Usage Baseline` fires.
Correlation CR-CDR-0016 raises one stitched compromised-workload-credential incident.

preventive_controls: Scope workload IAM roles to least privilege so a stolen credential cannot invoke Discovery/IAM actions outside the application's needs.
Prefer short-lived credentials (IMDSv2, IAM Roles Anywhere, session tokens) and rotate aggressively so an exposed credential has a narrow window of use.
Enforce a permissions boundary and SCP that denies IAM enumeration to workload identities.
detection_engineering: Let Cortex auto-tune ABIOCs against the learned per-identity cloud API usage baseline rather than hand-authoring static rules for individual API actions.
Alert on a workload identity whose API-call rate spikes above its learned baseline.
Alert on a workload identity invoking Discovery/IAM actions absent from its learned action set.
